description:
Wick is the household Natu who answers the child’s two taps and guesses the hidden button correctly. He waits for the next move in a private game. At the table his attention becomes much less mysterious: he inches closer and watches every journey of the fork.

An already familiar household individual. Choosing him extends a relationship that begins before the adventure.

The bedroom projection gives his game an uncanny scale. Its existence does not establish a link to Whyduck’s brain or the sea entities.

Proposed continuity after evolution: as Xatu, Wick no longer fits the little space beside the child’s pillow. He settles beside the bed and answers the same two taps against the floor. At a later shared meal, his long, solemn stillness ends when the fork moves. These repeated private habits make the taller creature recognizable without treating evolution as permission to disclose the future or explain the opening dream.
